claim: The autophagy-related E3 complex Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is recruited to the PAS via Atg16 interaction with Atg21, which binds phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) produced at the PAS.
source: Previous studies in yeast revealed that the autophagy-related E3 complex Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is recruited to the PAS via Atg16 interaction with Atg21, which binds phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) produced at the PAS, to stimulate conjugation of the ubiquitin-like protein Atg8 to phosphatidylethanolamine.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 complex stimulates conjugation of the ubiquitin-like protein Atg8 to phosphatidylethanolamine.
source: Previous studies in yeast revealed that the autophagy-related E3 complex Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is recruited to the PAS via Atg16 interaction with Atg21, which binds phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) produced at the PAS, to stimulate conjugation of the ubiquitin-like protein Atg8 to phosphatidylethanolamine.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and represents established knowledge.

claim: A novel mechanism for PAS targeting of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is mediated by the interaction of Atg12 with the Atg1 kinase complex.
source: Here, we discover a novel mechanism for the PAS targeting of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16, which is mediated by the interaction of Atg12 with the Atg1 kinase complex that serves as a scaffold for PAS organization.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Atg1 kinase complex serves as a scaffold for PAS organization.
source: Here, we discover a novel mechanism for the PAS targeting of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16, which is mediated by the interaction of Atg12 with the Atg1 kinase complex that serves as a scaffold for PAS organization.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Cells lacking both PI3P-dependent and Atg12-dependent mechanisms completely lose the PAS localization of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16.
source: While autophagy is partially defective without one of these mechanisms, cells lacking both completely lose the PAS localization of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 and show no autophagic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and other figures in the manuscript.

claim: Cells lacking both PI3P-dependent and Atg12-dependent mechanisms show no autophagic activity.
source: While autophagy is partially defective without one of these mechanisms, cells lacking both completely lose the PAS localization of Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 and show no autophagic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from ALP assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism stimulates Atg8 lipidation.
source: As with the PI3P-dependent mechanism, Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism stimulates Atg8 lipidation, but also has the specific function of facilitating PAS scaffold assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A demonstrating Atg8-PE production.

claim: Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism has the specific function of facilitating PAS scaffold assembly.
source: As with the PI3P-dependent mechanism, Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism stimulates Atg8 lipidation, but also has the specific function of facilitating PAS scaffold assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B and 4C demonstrating Atg17-GFP puncta formation.

claim: Autophagy is a major route for transport of intracellular material into lysosomes or vacuoles in almost all eukaryotes.
source: Macroautophagy (hereafter autophagy) is a major route for transport of intracellular material into lysosomes or vacuoles in almost all eukaryotes (Ohsumi, 2014; Yang and Klionsky, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and represents established knowledge.

claim: In autophagy, a membrane cisterna called the isolation membrane is generated, expands, becomes spherical, and closes to form a double membrane vesicle called the autophagosome.
source: In autophagy, a membrane cisterna called the isolation membrane (or phagophore) is generated, expands, becomes spherical, and closes to form a double membrane vesicle called the autophagosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the autophagy process.

claim: During autophagosome formation, various cytoplasmic components, including proteins, RNA, and organelles, are selectively or non-selectively sequestered into the autophagosome.
source: During the course of this process, various cytoplasmic components, including proteins, RNA, and organelles, are selectively or non-selectively sequestered into the autophagosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about autophagy function.

claim: The autophagosome fuses with the lysosome/vacuole to allow degradation of the contents.
source: The autophagosome fuses with the lysosome/vacuole to allow degradation of the contents.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the autophagy pathway.

claim: Autophagy is involved in the regulation of a wide range of cellular functions and linked to a variety of human diseases.
source: An increasing number of studies have suggested that autophagy is involved in the regulation of a wide range of cellular functions, and linked to a variety of human diseases (Bento et al., 2016; Dikic and Elazar, 2018; Mizushima, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Over 40 Atg proteins have been identified to date.
source: Among the over 40 Atg proteins that have been identified to date, 19 are directly involved in the biogenesis of the autophagosome induced under starvation (Nakatogawa et al., 2009; Ohsumi, 2014; Yang and Klionsky, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: 19 core Atg proteins are directly involved in the biogenesis of the autophagosome induced under starvation.
source: Among the over 40 Atg proteins that have been identified to date, 19 are directly involved in the biogenesis of the autophagosome induced under starvation (Nakatogawa et al., 2009; Ohsumi, 2014; Yang and Klionsky, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Core Atg proteins constitute six functional units: the Atg1 kinase complex, Atg9 vesicles, PI3K complex I, the Atg2-Atg18 complex, the Atg12 conjugation system, and the Atg8 conjugation system.
source: These 'core' Atg proteins constitute six functional units: (i) the Atg1 kinase complex; (ii) Atg9 vesicles; (iii) phosphatidylinositol (PI) 3-kinase (PI3K) complex I; (iv) the Atg2-Atg18 complex; (v) the Atg12 conjugation system; and (vi) the Atg8 conjugation system.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In response to starvation, Atg proteins interact with each other, localize to the site of autophagosome formation in an ordered manner, and organize the pre-autophagosomal structure (PAS).
source: In response to starvation, these proteins interact with each other, localize to the site of autophagosome formation in an ordered manner, and organize the pre-autophagosomal structure (PAS) (Nakatogawa et al., 2009; Suzuki et al., 2001; Suzuki and Ohsumi, 2010), in which a precursor of the autophagosomal membrane is generated.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A precursor of the autophagosomal membrane is generated at the PAS.
source: In response to starvation, these proteins interact with each other, localize to the site of autophagosome formation in an ordered manner, and organize the pre-autophagosomal structure (PAS) (Nakatogawa et al., 2009; Suzuki et al., 2001; Suzuki and Ohsumi, 2010), in which a precursor of the autophagosomal membrane is generated.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Atg12 is covalently attached to a lysine residue in Atg5 via ubiquitin-like conjugation reactions, resulting in the Atg12-Atg5 conjugate.
source: The ubiquitin-like protein Atg12 is covalently attached to a lysine residue in Atg5 via ubiquitin-like conjugation reactions, resulting in the Atg12-Atg5 conjugate (Mizushima et al., 1998a; Mizushima et al., 1998b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Atg12-Atg5 non-covalently interacts with Atg16 to form the Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 complex.
source: Atg12-Atg5 non-covalently interacts with Atg16 (Atg16L in mammals) to form the Atg12-Atg5-Atg16/Atg16L complex (hereafter the Atg16/Atg16L complex) (Kuma et al., 2002; Mizushima et al., 2003; Mizushima et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Atg16/Atg16L complex is localized to the PAS and acts as an E3 enzyme to stimulate the conjugation reaction of ubiquitin-like Atg8/LC3-family proteins to the lipid phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) in autophagosome intermediates.
source: The Atg16/Atg16L complex is localized to the PAS (or the site of autophagosome formation) and acts as an E3 enzyme to stimulate the conjugation reaction of ubiquitin-like Atg8/LC3-family proteins to the lipid phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) in autophagosome intermediates (i.e., a still-unknown membrane component of the PAS and the isolation membrane) (Suzuki et al., 2007; Hanada et al., 2007; Ichimura et al., 2000; Fujita et al., 2008; Nakatogawa, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Atg8-PE conjugates promote the expansion of the isolation membrane.
source: Atg8-PE conjugates promote the expansion of the isolation membrane (Nakatogawa et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2008), and also bind to autophagy receptors that recognize specific degradation targets for their selective sequestration into the autophagosome (Gatica et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Atg8-PE conjugates bind to autophagy receptors that recognize specific degradation targets for their selective sequestration into the autophagosome.
source: Atg8-PE conjugates promote the expansion of the isolation membrane (Nakatogawa et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2008), and also bind to autophagy receptors that recognize specific degradation targets for their selective sequestration into the autophagosome (Gatica et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In both yeast and mammals, the recruitment of the Atg16/Atg16L complex to the site of autophagosome formation depends on PI3P produced by PI3K complex I.
source: In both yeast and mammals, the recruitment of the Atg16/Atg16L complex to the site of autophagosome formation depends on PI3-phosphate (PI3P) produced by PI3K complex I (Itakura and Mizushima, 2010; Suzuki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In mammalian cells, WIPI2b binds both Atg16L1 and PI3P to target the Atg16L1 complex to autophagosome formation sites.
source: A recent study in mammalian cells revealed that the PROPPIN family protein WIPI2b binds both Atg16L1 and PI3P to target the Atg16L1 complex to autophagosome formation sites (Dooley et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, Atg21 mediates the recruitment of the Atg16 complex to the PAS in a manner similar to WIPI2b in mammals.
source: In S. cerevisiae, Atg21, one of the three WIPI homologs, was shown to mediate this process in a similar manner (Juris et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Knockout of ATG21 did not completely abrogate the PAS localization of the Atg16 complex or the autophagic activity of cells.
source: However, knockout of ATG21 did not completely abrogate the PAS localization of the Atg16 complex or the autophagic activity of cells (Meiling-Wesse et al., 2004; Nair et al., 2010; Strømhaug et al., 2004), suggesting that there is an unknown mechanism which directs the Atg16 complex to the PAS, in addition to the PI3K complex I-PI3P-Atg21 axis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is an unknown mechanism which directs the Atg16 complex to the PAS, in addition to the PI3K complex I-PI3P-Atg21 axis.
source: However, knockout of ATG21 did not completely abrogate the PAS localization of the Atg16 complex or the autophagic activity of cells (Meiling-Wesse et al., 2004; Nair et al., 2010; Strømhaug et al., 2004), suggesting that there is an unknown mechanism which directs the Atg16 complex to the PAS, in addition to the PI3K complex I-PI3P-Atg21 axis.
evidence: This is an inference based on previous experimental observations cited in the text.

claim: The PAS localization of Atg5 was lost by deletion of ATG16.
source: In agreement with this model, the PAS localization of Atg5 was lost by deletion of ATG16 (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Atg5 localized to the PAS less efficiently in the absence of Atg21.
source: It was also confirmed that Atg5 localized to the PAS less efficiently in the absence of Atg21.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Deletion of ATG14 decreased the PAS localization of Atg5.
source: Deletion of ATG14 decreased the PAS localization of Atg5; however, Atg5 still significantly localized to the PAS even without Atg14, to an extent similar to that observed in cells lacking Atg21.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Atg5 still significantly localized to the PAS even without Atg14, to an extent similar to that observed in cells lacking Atg21.
source: Deletion of ATG14 decreased the PAS localization of Atg5; however, Atg5 still significantly localized to the PAS even without Atg14, to an extent similar to that observed in cells lacking Atg21.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The frequency of Atg5 localization to the PAS was decreased in the absence of Atg12, although it abnormally accumulated at the PAS.
source: In addition, we noticed that the frequency of Atg5 localization to the PAS was decreased in the absence of Atg12, although it abnormally accumulated at the PAS.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: PAS localization of Atg5 was totally abolished in cells lacking both Atg14 and Atg12.
source: We found that PAS localization of Atg5 was totally abolished in cells lacking both Atg14 and Atg12 (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Disruption of ATG12 abrogated the residual PAS localization of Atg5 in ATG21 knockout cells.
source: Disruption of ATG12 also abrogated the residual PAS localization of Atg5 in ATG21 knockout cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: There exists an uncharacterized, PI3P-independent mechanism that targets the Atg16 complex to the PAS, which likely involves Atg12.
source: These results suggest that in addition to the previously described PI3P-dependent pathway, there exists an uncharacterized, PI3P-independent mechanism that targets the Atg16 complex to the PAS, which likely involves Atg12.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Mass spectrometry of Atg5-FLAG immunoprecipitates identified most components of the Atg1 complex as possible interaction partners of the Atg16 complex.
source: Mass spectrometry of the immunoprecipitates identified a number of proteins as possible interaction partners of the Atg16 complex, and included most components of the Atg1 complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Atg1, Atg17, and Atg29 could be detected in Atg5-FLAG immunoprecipitates by immunoblotting.
source: Atg1, Atg17, and Atg29 could also be detected in Atg5-FLAG immunoprecipitates by immunoblotting (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Coimmunoprecipitation of Atg17 with Atg5-FLAG was largely decreased when ATG12 or ATG16 was deleted.
source: When ATG12 or ATG16 was deleted, coimmunoprecipitation of Atg17 with Atg5-FLAG was largely decreased (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Atg17 was not precipitated with Atg5-FLAG in the absence of Atg10.
source: We also showed that Atg17 was not precipitated with Atg5-FLAG in the absence of Atg10, which is essential for Atg12 conjugation to Atg5 (Mizushima et al., 1998a) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Atg10 is essential for Atg12 conjugation to Atg5.
source: We also showed that Atg17 was not precipitated with Atg5-FLAG in the absence of Atg10, which is essential for Atg12 conjugation to Atg5 (Mizushima et al., 1998a) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of FLAG-tagged Atg16 precipitated Atg17, but this was lost by knockout of ATG5 or ATG12.
source: Immunoprecipitation of FLAG-tagged Atg16 also precipitated Atg17; however, this was lost by knockout of ATG5 or ATG12 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The formation of the Atg16 complex is required for its interaction with the Atg1 complex.
source: Thus, the formation of the Atg16 complex is required for its interaction with the Atg1 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: All the components of the Atg1 complex are important for its interaction with the Atg16 complex.
source: The results clearly showed that all the components of the Atg1 complex are important for its interaction with the Atg16 complex (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The F430A mutation in Atg13 reduced Atg17 precipitation with the Atg16 complex.
source: In addition, the F430A mutation in Atg13, which impairs the formation of the Atg1 complex (Yamamoto et al., 2016), reduced Atg17 precipitation with the Atg16 complex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The F430A mutation in Atg13 impairs the formation of the Atg1 complex.
source: In addition, the F430A mutation in Atg13, which impairs the formation of the Atg1 complex (Yamamoto et al., 2016), reduced Atg17 precipitation with the Atg16 complex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The formation of the Atg1 complex is a prerequisite for its association with the Atg16 complex.
source: These results suggest that the formation of the Atg1 complex is a prerequisite for its association with the Atg16 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: ATG14 deletion did not affect Atg17 precipitation with Atg5-FLAG.
source: In contrast, ATG14 deletion did not affect Atg17 precipitation with Atg5-FLAG (Figure 2E), consistent with the idea that this novel intercomplex interaction is involved in the PI3P-independent PAS targeting of the Atg16 complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The Atg16 complex interacts with the Atg1 complex depending on cell treatment with rapamycin.
source: We found that the Atg16 complex interacts with the Atg1 complex depending on cell treatment with rapamycin (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The interaction between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes was not considerably decreased by the absence of Atg11.
source: Consistent with this result, the interaction was not considerably decreased by the absence of Atg11, which binds to the Atg1 complex but is dispensable for starvation-induced autophagy (Kamada et al., 2000; Kim et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: Atg11 binds to the Atg1 complex but is dispensable for starvation-induced autophagy.
source: Consistent with this result, the interaction was not considerably decreased by the absence of Atg11, which binds to the Atg1 complex but is dispensable for starvation-induced autophagy (Kamada et al., 2000; Kim et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Upon nutrient starvation, Atg1, Atg13, and the Atg17-Atg29-Atg31 complex form the Atg1 complex, and multiple copies of the complex further associate with each other, leading to activation of Atg1 kinase via intermolecular autophosphorylation.
source: Upon nutrient starvation, Atg1, Atg13, and the Atg17-Atg29-Atg31 complex form the Atg1 complex, and multiple copies of the complex further associate with each other, leading to activation of Atg1 kinase via intermolecular autophosphorylation (Yamamoto et al., 2016; Yeh et al., 2011; Yeh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The assemblage of the Atg1 complexes serves as a scaffold to recruit downstream Atg proteins for PAS organization.
source: This assemblage of the Atg1 complexes serves as a scaffold to recruit downstream Atg proteins for PAS organization.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on previous studies.

claim: The interaction between the Atg16 complex and the Atg1 complex was lost in the F375A mutant of Atg13.
source: The interaction between the Atg16 complex and the Atg1 complex was lost in the F375A mutant of Atg13 (Figure 2D), which can form the Atg1 complex, but is defective in its higher order assembly (Yamamoto et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The F375A mutant of Atg13 can form the Atg1 complex, but is defective in its higher order assembly.
source: The interaction between the Atg16 complex and the Atg1 complex was lost in the F375A mutant of Atg13 (Figure 2D), which can form the Atg1 complex, but is defective in its higher order assembly (Yamamoto et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The D211A mutation in Atg1, which abolishes its kinase activity, did not affect the interaction between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes.
source: By contrast, the D211A mutation in Atg1, which abolishes its kinase activity (Matsuura et al., 1997), did not affect the interaction between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The D211A mutation in Atg1 abolishes its kinase activity.
source: By contrast, the D211A mutation in Atg1, which abolishes its kinase activity (Matsuura et al., 1997), did not affect the interaction between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The Atg16 complex associates with the Atg1 complex following its supramolecular assembly in a manner independent of Atg1 kinase activity.
source: These results suggest that the Atg16 complex associates with the Atg1 complex following its supramolecular assembly in a manner independent of Atg1 kinase activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 2D and 2G.

claim: Yeast two-hybrid assay suggested that Atg12 could bind Atg17 and Atg31.
source: Yeast two-hybrid assay suggested that Atg12 could bind Atg17 and Atg31 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Atg12-Atg17 interaction was still observed in atg13Δ atg31Δ cells.
source: In this assay, the Atg12-Atg17 interaction was still observed in atg13Δ atg31Δ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), in which Atg17 should not interact with the remaining subunits Atg1 and Atg29.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The Atg12-Atg31 interaction was abolished by ATG17 knockout.
source: By contrast, the Atg12-Atg31 interaction was abolished by ATG17 knockout, suggesting that Atg12 interacted with Atg31 via Atg17 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Atg12 interacted with Atg31 via Atg17.
source: By contrast, the Atg12-Atg31 interaction was abolished by ATG17 knockout, suggesting that Atg12 interacted with Atg31 via Atg17 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of Atg12-GFP coprecipitated Atg17 in cells lacking the other four subunits of the Atg1 complex, when both Atg12-GFP and Atg17 were overexpressed.
source: In addition, immunoprecipitation of Atg12 C-terminally fused with GFP, which is not associated with Atg5 and Atg16, coprecipitated Atg17 in cells lacking the other four subunits of the Atg1 complex, when both of Atg12-GFP and Atg17 were overexpressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The interaction between Atg17 and Atg12 mediates the association of the two complexes.
source: These results suggest that the interaction between Atg17 and Atg12 mediates the association of the two complexes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from yeast two-hybrid and immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: A previous study reported that while the ubiquitin-like domain of Atg12 was essential for autophagy, deletion of the N-terminal region caused a partial defect.
source: A previous study reported that while the ubiquitin-like domain of Atg12 was essential for autophagy, deletion of the N-terminal region caused a partial defect (Hanada and Ohsumi, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The N-terminal region of Atg12 was not required for Atg12 conjugation to Atg5, the E3 activity of the conjugate, or the interaction of the conjugate with Atg16.
source: The N-terminal region of Atg12 was not required for Atg12 conjugation to Atg5, the E3 activity of the conjugate, or the interaction of the conjugate with Atg16 (Hanada and Ohsumi, 2005) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Atg1 complex was hardly coimmunoprecipitated with the Atg16 complex that contained Atg12 lacking the N-terminal 56 residues (Atg12ΔN56).
source: We found that the Atg1 complex was hardly coimmunoprecipitated with the Atg16 complex that contained Atg12 lacking the N-terminal 56 residues (Atg12ΔN56) (Figure 3A), suggesting that the Atg12 N-terminal region is involved in the interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Atg12 N-terminal region is involved in the interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex.
source: We found that the Atg1 complex was hardly coimmunoprecipitated with the Atg16 complex that contained Atg12 lacking the N-terminal 56 residues (Atg12ΔN56) (Figure 3A), suggesting that the Atg12 N-terminal region is involved in the interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of wild-type Atg12 rescued a defect in the PAS localization of Atg5-GFP in atg21Δ atg12Δ cells.
source: While expression of wild-type Atg12 rescued a defect in the PAS localization of Atg5-GFP in atg21Δ atg12Δ cells, expression of the Atg12ΔN56 mutant did not (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Expression of the Atg12ΔN56 mutant did not rescue a defect in the PAS localization of Atg5-GFP in atg21Δ atg12Δ cells.
source: While expression of wild-type Atg12 rescued a defect in the PAS localization of Atg5-GFP in atg21Δ atg12Δ cells, expression of the Atg12ΔN56 mutant did not (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: atg12ΔN56 cells and atg21Δ cells were only partially defective in autophagy.
source: Consistent with previous results (Hanada and Ohsumi, 2005; Meiling-Wesse et al., 2004; Strømhaug et al., 2004), atg12ΔN56 cells (atg12Δ cells carrying the atg12ΔN56 plasmid) and atg21Δ cells (atg21Δ atg12Δ cells carrying the ATG12WT plasmid) were only partially defective in autophagy (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and citations to previous studies.

claim: When atg12ΔN56 and atg21Δ mutations were combined, the cells showed almost no autophagic activity.
source: When these mutations were combined (atg21Δ atg12Δ cells carrying the atg12ΔN56 plasmid), the cells showed almost no autophagic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex acts to target the Atg16 complex to the PAS.
source: These results suggest that the interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex indeed acts to target the Atg16 complex to the PAS, and that defects caused by the absence of this interaction can be partly compensated by the PI3P-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Defects caused by the absence of the Atg12-dependent interaction can be partly compensated by the PI3P-dependent mechanism.
source: These results suggest that the interaction of the Atg16 complex with the Atg1 complex indeed acts to target the Atg16 complex to the PAS, and that defects caused by the absence of this interaction can be partly compensated by the PI3P-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: If both the Atg12-dependent and PI3P-dependent mechanisms are simultaneously compromised, cells totally lose their ability to form the autophagosome.
source: If both of these mechanisms are simultaneously compromized, cells totally lose their ability to form the autophagosome.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: PI3P-dependent PAS recruitment of the Atg16 complex is important for the production of Atg8-PE.
source: Previous studies showed that PI3P-dependent PAS recruitment of the Atg16 complex is important for the production of Atg8-PE (Meiling-Wesse et al., 2004; Strømhaug et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Atg8-PE production is stimulated upon nitrogen starvation.
source: Atg8-PE production is stimulated upon nitrogen starvation (Figure 4A, atg12Δ/pATG12WT).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ATG21 knockout significantly reduced the level of Atg8-PE, which still gradually increased during nitrogen starvation.
source: As reported previously (Meiling-Wesse et al., 2004; Strømhaug et al., 2004), ATG21 knockout significantly reduced the level of Atg8-PE, which still gradually increased during nitrogen starvation (atg21Δ atg12Δ/pATG12WT).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and citations to previous studies.

claim: Deletion of the N-terminal region of Atg12 partially decreased Atg8-PE formation.
source: We found that deletion of the N-terminal region of Atg12 also partially decreased Atg8-PE formation (atg12Δ/patg12ΔN56).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Starvation-induced Atg8-PE formation was totally abolished in cells lacking both Atg21 and the N-terminal region of Atg12.
source: In addition, starvation-induced Atg8-PE formation was totally abolished in cells lacking both Atg21 and the N-terminal region of Atg12 (atg21Δ atg12Δ/patg12ΔN56).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The residual amount of Atg8-PE in cells lacking both Atg21 and the N-terminal region of Atg12 represents conjugates produced in the vacuolar membrane depending on the Atg16 complex, which is dispersed throughout the cytoplasm, independent of autophagy.
source: Of note, the residual amount of Atg8-PE in these mutant cells should represent the conjugates that were produced in the vacuolar membrane depending on the Atg16 complex, which is dispersed throughout the cytoplasm, independent of autophagy (Nakatogawa et al., 2012a).
evidence: This is an inference based on previous knowledge cited in the text.

claim: The Atg16 complex recruited by the Atg12-dependent mechanism acts as an E3 enzyme and promotes Atg8 lipidation.
source: These results demonstrated that the Atg16 complex recruited by the Atg12-dependent mechanism acts as an E3 enzyme and promotes Atg8 lipidation, as was observed with the PI3P-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Atg17-GFP puncta were decreased by knockout of ATG12.
source: We noticed that Atg17-GFP puncta, which represent PAS scaffold assembly (Yamamoto et al., 2016), were decreased by knockout of ATG12, which disrupts the Atg12-dependent mechanism, whereas the puncta were increased by knockout of ATG14 or ATG21, which impairs the PI3P-dependent mechanism (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Atg17-GFP puncta were increased by knockout of ATG14 or ATG21.
source: We noticed that Atg17-GFP puncta, which represent PAS scaffold assembly (Yamamoto et al., 2016), were decreased by knockout of ATG12, which disrupts the Atg12-dependent mechanism, whereas the puncta were increased by knockout of ATG14 or ATG21, which impairs the PI3P-dependent mechanism (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Atg17-GFP puncta represent PAS scaffold assembly.
source: We noticed that Atg17-GFP puncta, which represent PAS scaffold assembly (Yamamoto et al., 2016), were decreased by knockout of ATG12, which disrupts the Atg12-dependent mechanism, whereas the puncta were increased by knockout of ATG14 or ATG21, which impairs the PI3P-dependent mechanism (Figure 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The formation of Atg17-GFP puncta upon rapamycin treatment was defective in the absence of Atg12, Atg5, or Atg16.
source: The results demonstrated that the formation of Atg17-GFP puncta upon rapamycin treatment was defective in the absence of Atg12, Atg5, or Atg16 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Atg17-GFP puncta were decreased by deletion of the N-terminal region of Atg12.
source: More importantly, Atg17-GFP puncta were also decreased by deletion of the N-terminal region of Atg12 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The Atg16 complex recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism facilitates starvation-induced PAS scaffold assembly.
source: These results suggest that the Atg16 complex recruited via the Atg12-dependent mechanism (i.e., the interaction with the Atg1 complex) facilitates starvation-induced PAS scaffold assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: Disruption of ATG21 or ATG14 did not totally abolish PAS localization of the Atg16 complex.
source: However, disruption of ATG21 or ATG14 did not totally abolish PAS localization of the Atg16 complex, suggesting the existence of another pathway that targets this complex to the PAS in a PI3P-independent manner.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on previous studies and confirmed by data in Figure 1.

claim: The Atg16 complex is recruited to the PAS through two different pathways.
source: In this study, we discovered that the Atg16 complex also interacts with the Atg1 complex via the N-terminal region of Atg12 to localize to the PAS (Figure 5, Atg12-dependent targeting). Thus, the Atg16 complex is recruited to the PAS through two different pathways.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: In the absence of both PI3P-dependent and Atg12-dependent pathways, the Atg16 complex hardly localized to the PAS, and autophagy was completely blocked.
source: Although disrupting either of the pathways caused partial defects, in the absence of both of these pathways, the Atg16 complex hardly localized to the PAS, and autophagy was completely blocked.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, 3B, and 3C.

claim: The PI3P-dependent and Atg12-dependent pathways function in a partially redundant manner.
source: These results suggested that these pathways function in a partially redundant manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: The PI3P-dependent and Atg12-dependent pathways cooperatively act to stimulate Atg8-PE formation in response to starvation.
source: Consistent with this idea, we showed that these pathways cooperatively act to stimulate Atg8-PE formation in response to starvation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The Atg1 complex serves as a scaffold to initiate PAS organization, whereas Atg21 is recruited at a later step, following the production of PI3P by PI3K complex I.
source: However, the Atg1 complex serves as a scaffold to initiate PAS organization, whereas Atg21 is recruited at a later step, following the production of PI3P by PI3K complex I (Figure 5), suggesting that there is a functional difference between these pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge and inference based on the temporal order of events.

claim: The Atg12-dependent pathway, but not the PI3P-dependent pathway, is involved in PAS scaffold assembly.
source: Indeed, we found that the Atg12-dependent pathway, but not the PI3P-dependent pathway, is involved in PAS scaffold assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: The Atg16 complex recruited by the Atg12-dependent pathway has a specific, non-E3 role in the initiation of PAS organization.
source: Thus, the Atg16 complex recruited by the Atg12-dependent pathway has a specific, non-E3 role in the initiation of PAS organization.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing PAS scaffold assembly function.

claim: The Atg16 complex recruited through the association of the Atg1 complex likely contributes to Atg8 lipidation at later stages.
source: Given the complementary relationship with the PI3P-dependent pathway, it is likely that the Atg16 complex recruited through the association of the Atg1 complex also contributes to Atg8 lipidation at later stages (Figure 5, dashed arrow).
evidence: This is speculation based on the complementary nature of the two pathways.

claim: The interaction between the Atg16 complex and the Atg1 complex required both of the complexes to be intact.
source: The interaction between the Atg16 complex and the Atg1 complex required both of the complexes to be intact.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A, 2B, and 2C.

claim: Higher order assembly of Atg1 complexes was a prerequisite for the interaction with the Atg16 complex.
source: In addition, higher order assembly of Atg1 complexes was a prerequisite for the interaction (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The Atg16 complex, in which Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is dimerized by the homodimerization of Atg16, simultaneously binds to two copies of the Atg1 complexes via the N-terminal regions of Atg12.
source: We speculate that the Atg16 complex, in which Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is dimerized by the homodimerization of Atg16 (Fujioka et al., 2010), simultaneously binds to two copies of the Atg1 complexes via the N-terminal regions of Atg12 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural properties of the complexes and experimental data.

claim: Atg16 homodimerizes.
source: We speculate that the Atg16 complex, in which Atg12-Atg5-Atg16 is dimerized by the homodimerization of Atg16 (Fujioka et al., 2010), simultaneously binds to two copies of the Atg1 complexes via the N-terminal regions of Atg12 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The mode of interaction between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes can crosslink the Atg1 complexes, resulting in the facilitation of supramolecular assembly of Atg1 complexes to form the PAS scaffold.
source: This mode of interaction can crosslink the Atg1 complexes, resulting in the facilitation of supramolecular assembly of Atg1 complexes to form the PAS scaffold.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed model of interaction.

claim: The association between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes requires the N-terminal region of Atg12.
source: In this study, we showed that the association between the Atg16 and Atg1 complexes requires the N-terminal region of Atg12.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is no sequence similarity between the N-terminal regions of yeast and mammalian Atg12.
source: Although there is no sequence similarity between the N-terminal regions of yeast and mammalian Atg12, a recent study revealed that the Atg16L complex also associates with the ULK1 complex (corresponding to the Atg1 complex) in mammalian cells (Nishimura et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: The Atg16L complex associates with the ULK1 complex in mammalian cells.
source: Although there is no sequence similarity between the N-terminal regions of yeast and mammalian Atg12, a recent study revealed that the Atg16L complex also associates with the ULK1 complex (corresponding to the Atg1 complex) in mammalian cells (Nishimura et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The intercomplex association between Atg16L and ULK1 complexes was mediated by the interaction between Atg16L and FIP200.
source: This intercomplex association was mediated by the interaction between Atg16L and FIP200, which is a mammalian counterpart of yeast Atg17, and important for the localization of the Atg16L complex to the isolation membrane.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: FIP200 is a mammalian counterpart of yeast Atg17.
source: This intercomplex association was mediated by the interaction between Atg16L and FIP200, which is a mammalian counterpart of yeast Atg17, and important for the localization of the Atg16L complex to the isolation membrane.
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: The interaction between Atg16L and FIP200 is important for the localization of the Atg16L complex to the isolation membrane.
source: This intercomplex association was mediated by the interaction between Atg16L and FIP200, which is a mammalian counterpart of yeast Atg17, and important for the localization of the Atg16L complex to the isolation membrane.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The recruitment of the Atg16/Atg16L complex to autophagosome intermediates through association with the Atg1/ULK1 complex is a common process during autophagosome formation in yeast and mammals.
source: Thus, although the underlying mechanisms are different, the recruitment of the Atg16/Atg16L complex to autophagosome intermediates through association with the Atg1/ULK1 complex is a common process during autophagosome formation in yeast and mammals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of yeast and mammalian systems.

claim: It is unclear how the Atg16L-ULK1 association cooperates with the PI3P (WIPI2)-dependent mechanism in mammalian cells.
source: It is still unclear how this process cooperates with the PI3P (WIPI2)-dependent mechanism in mammalian cells.
evidence: This acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The Atg16L complex may facilitate supramolecular assembly of ULK complexes in the initiation of autophagosome formation.
source: The Atg16L complex may also facilitate supramolecular assembly of ULK complexes in the initiation of autophagosome formation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings in yeast.

claim: Rapamycin inhibits Tor kinase complex 1 and thereby induces various starvation responses including autophagy even in the presence of nutrients.
source: Yeast cells expressing FLAG-tagged Atg5 (Atg5-FLAG) were treated with rapamycin, which inhibits Tor kinase complex 1 and thereby induces various starvation responses including autophagy even in the presence of nutrients (Noda and Ohsumi, 1998), followed by immunoprecipitation using anti-FLAG antibody.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.
